 War clouds and the ballot box
 The prospect of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran has acquired an ominous dimension with Tehran warning of an ‘apocalyptic war’ if attacked again (Front page October 25). With Israel’s October 27 elections and the U.S. midterm approaching on November 3, the timing of further escalation invites serious scrutiny. Are electoral calculations overshadowing the pursuit of peace? The Trump-Netanyahu equation too warrants serious questioning. Whipping up war hysteria, nationalist fervour and anti-Palestinian sentiment through military confrontation may serve electoral calculations but it comes at an appalling human cost. The suspicion that the Epstein controversy may be influencing Mr. Trump’s calculations deserve scrutiny but the allegations of Netanayahu blackmailing remain unsubstantiated and must not be presented as fact. Iran’s threat to retaliate against Gulf states, energy infrastructure and vital shipping routes underscore the catastrophic risks of renewed escalation. A war intended to demonstrate brutal strength could engulf the region, disrupt global energy supplies and exact a devastating civilian toll . When decisions of war and peace coincide with leaders’ electoral interests, transparency and accountability become imperative. If military action is driven by political survival than any demonstrable necessity, it is not strength but a reckless gamble with millions of innocent lives. The ballot box must never become a license to turn the battlefield into an instrument of political survival. The UN and the International community must urgently unite to halt this perilous march towards a wider war.
 M. Jameel Ahmed,
 Mysuru
 Red alert, blue skies
 The accuracy of meteorological forecasts for Tamil Nadu, especially regarding rainfall and storms in the Bay of Bengal during the monsoon season, seems to miss the mark. A recent case was the ‘red alert’ issued for the southern districts of Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli. In anticipation of potential devastation, the District Collectors declared a holiday for all educational institutions. Fortunately, we experienced bright sunshine instead. However, this required educational institutions to conduct compensatory classes the following Saturday. While the administration must prioritise safety, the frequent discrepancy between official forecasts and actual weather conditions creates unnecessary disruption. Interestingly, independent private weather bloggers often provide more accurate localised forecasts.
 Rajakumar Arulanandham,
 Palayamkottai, Tamil Nadu
 Vaulting to new heights
 It was inspiring to read the report about 19-year-old Chuki Birda from Rajasthan, who has set a national pole vault record at the 41st National junior athletics championships in Chennai (‘Sport’ page, October 25). Such stories deserve wider attention given the discrimination girls still face in parts of India.
 M.N. Saraswathi Devi,
 Secunderabad
